scoring_justification: Full recompute of the thermoelectric simulation and efficiency solver is infeasible in the lightweight verifier; scoring uses structural ranking of doping-performance relationships in the CSV and result-level comparison of trade-off percentages to the paper's reported 19% and 16% within ±3% tolerance.

hidden_assets.purpose: gold percentages for result-level comparison of the trade-off between peak ZT and efficiency
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper 'ZT Optimization: An Application Focus' (Materials 2017, 10, 309), Section 4, Silicide Based Material: 'despite the potential 19% increase in peak ZT, optimizing purely for peak ZT could result in a 16% lower performance than optimizing for the best average ZT.'
hidden_assets.generation_method: verbatim extraction from the published paper; values are 19% (peak_ZT_increase_pct) and 16% (efficiency_decrease_pct).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: the paper's central quantitative claim that the reproduction task must match; these numbers are published and verifiable.

outputs.description: Per‑doping raw data; checker verifies doping ranking (efficiency‑optimal doping yields lower peak_ZT and higher average_ZT).
Quantified trade‑off; checker compares peak_ZT_increase_pct and efficiency_decrease_pct to paper‑reported 19% and 16% within tolerance.

output_contract.notes: The task reproduces the silicide trade‑off between peak ZT and single‑leg efficiency using the paper’s two‑parabolic‑band model with given parameters. The checker validates structural ranking and tightens result‑level comparison on the trade‑off percentages.
